newsitem.title: UK: UK raises 224 million pounds from AEA Technology.
newsitem.headline: UK raises 224 million pounds from AEA Technology.

text.p: Britain on Wednesday valued AEA Technology at 224 million pounds ($349 million), setting the flotation price of the former science and engineering services arm of the Atomic Energy Authority at 280 pence per share.
The shares are due to start trading in London on Thursday.
The shares had been expected to be priced between 240 pence and 270p, raising up to 216 million pounds for the government.
But a rush for shares prompted the government on Tuesday to accept a recommendation from its advisers, merchant bank Schroders, and raise the indicative price range by 10p to between 250p and 280p.
The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said the offer had been about seven times oversubscribed.
Because of the strong interest from institutions, it had raised its allocation to intermediaries to 12.5 percent of the company's share capital from 10 percent, the DTI said.

Applications for shares had been scaled down and allocated to about 22 percent of the amount requested up to a ceiling of 7.5 million pounds, it added. "We look forward to life in the private sector and to building a successful business for the benefit of investors, customers and employees," said AEA Technology chairman Sir Anthony Cleaver in a statement."

AEA Technology works the public and private sectors to improve the efficiency of power stations and processes, to meet safety requirements and to manage nuclear and environmental challenges more effectively. ($1=.6420 Pound)
